string-array.name: help_ecu_voltage
string-array.item: System voltage at the engine ECU\'s power supply.

12.4–12.7 V with the engine off, usually 13.5–14.7 V with it running. Many modern cars (GM calls it RVC) charge \"smart\": with a full battery the alternator drops to 12.5–13 V. So a healthy car can show the voltage moving around while driving.
One low reading says nothing. It\'s bad if the voltage stays below 13 V and the cluster shows a charging warning, or the modules have power codes (P0562, for example).

string-array.name: help_adapter_voltage
string-array.item: Voltage at pin 16 of the OBD port, measured by the adapter.
A little lower than \"Voltage (ECU)\" because of the wiring to the port.
If it\'s far from the ECU value, check the OBD port, ground and the diagnostic fuse. Cheap ELM327 clones sometimes measure badly; then trust the ECU value.

string-array.name: help_ambient
string-array.item: Outside air temperature, reported by the engine ECU.
Close to the real thing while driving. Reads high when stopped and after a drive: the sensor picks up heat from the engine and the road.
−40 °C almost always means an open sensor circuit.

string-array.name: help_baro
string-array.item: About 101 kPa at sea level, about 1.2 kPa lower for every 100 m up. Weather moves it by a couple of kPa.
Far from what you\'d expect at your altitude means a bad sensor. The mixture depends on this value.
